title: Independent National Security Legislation Monitor Repeal Bill 2014
short_title: Independent National Security Legislation Monitor Repeal Bill 2014

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would abolish the Independent National Security Legislation Monitor and repeal the legislation establishing its role in reviewing counter-terrorism and national security laws.
It would transfer the office's records to the Department of Prime Minister and Cabinet while retaining arrangements for the Monitor's final annual report.
The repeal would begin on the later of 21 April 2014 and the day after Royal Assent, after the current Monitor's term expired.
changes: Protection from criminal and civil liability would continue for people served notices before commencement.
Existing immunity from legal action would be preserved.
The final report would have to be tabled in each House within 15 sitting days after the Prime Minister received it.
summary.affected: The Monitor and people served notices would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Scott Morrison
speeches.brief: Moved, on behalf of the Parliamentary Secretary to the Prime Minister, to discharge the resumption of debate on the Independent National Security Legislation Monitor Repeal Bill 2014 from the notice paper.
